hook: Timnit Gebru is a computer scientist who has become one of the most prominent voices in AI ethics and accountability. She earned her PhD in computer vision from Stanford University, advised by Fei-Fei Li, after early work in circuit design and audio engineering at Apple. She then completed a postdoctoral fellowship in Microsoft Research's Fairness, Accountability, Transparency and Ethics group before joining Google in 2018, where she co-led the Ethical AI research team with Margaret Mitchell. Gebru left Google in December 2020 after a dispute over a research paper examining the risks of large language models, a departure that drew wide attention to tensions between AI ethics researchers and corporate priorities. In December 2021 she founded the Distributed AI Research Institute, an independent, interdisciplinary institute with researchers based across North America, Europe and Africa that studies the harms of current AI systems and researches alternative approaches. She also co-founded Black in AI, a nonprofit supporting Black researchers and students in artificial intelligence.

quick_facts: Earned a PhD in computer vision from Stanford University, advised by Fei-Fei Li
Co-led Google's Ethical AI research team from 2018 until her December 2020 departure
Founded the Distributed AI Research Institute (DAIR) in December 2021 and serves as its executive director
Co-founded Black in AI to support Black researchers and students in artificial intelligence
Earlier career included circuit design and audio engineering work at Apple, and a postdoctoral fellowship at Microsoft Research's FATE group
Named to Time's 100 Most Influential People in 2022 and the BBC's 100 Women in 2023

achievements.title: Co-lead, Ethical AI team at Google
achievements.impact: Helped build one of the first corporate research teams focused on the fairness and social impact of AI systems, before her departure became a widely covered flashpoint in the industry.

achievements.impact: Built an independent research institute studying AI harms and alternative, community centered approaches, with researchers distributed across multiple continents.

achievements.title: Co-founder, Black in AI

achievements.title: Contributor to bias research in computer vision
achievements.impact: Contributed to research documenting demographic bias in commercial AI systems, work that influenced industry discussion of fairness testing.
